paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Abraham got scared and said Sarah was his sister, and the whole mess landed on a king who hadn't gone near her. But look who steps in: God says, "I have kept you from sinning against Me…" (Genesis 20:6) Abraham's plan wasn't what protected her, God was.

Now here's the part that gets me. Abraham told Abimelech he thought, "Surely there is no fear of God in this place." (Genesis 20:11) He guessed wrong, because Abimelech got up early the next morning and told his servants everything (Genesis 20:8). I've been dead sure a batch would burn and it came out fine, so I know fear makes us GREAT at being sure.

And then God uses the very man who messed up. God calls Abraham a prophet who will pray for Abimelech (Genesis 20:7), and Abraham prays, and God heals (Genesis 20:17). Abraham didn't earn that spot, and God still trusted him with it. So when you stumble, baker, God doesn't toss you aside, and Abraham's story isn't done, and neither is yours.
